test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements related to the Constitution of India is true?

options.text: Fundamental Rights set social and economic democracy, while Directive Principles establish political democracy.
Fundamental Rights are moral and political sanctions, but Directive Principles are legal sanctions.
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, whereas Directive Principles of State are non-justiciable.
Fundamental Rights promote the welfare of the community, while Directive Principles promote individual welfare.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Rights are justiciable, whereas Directive Principles of State are non-justiciable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are enforceable by the courts and can be challenged if violated. This means individuals can approach the judiciary if they feel their Fundamental Rights are infringed.
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** (DPSP), on the other hand, are guidelines for the state to follow in governance and policy-making but are not legally enforceable in a court of law.
 
• Fundamental Rights are primarily aimed at ensuring individual freedoms and rights, while DPSP are aimed at establishing a welfare state and achieving social and economic democracy.
 
• The conflict between Fundamental Rights and DPSP has been a subject of judicial interpretation, with courts balancing the need to protect individual rights with the aim to promote socio-economic welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35).
 
• They are justiciable, meaning they can be enforced through the judiciary.
 
• Include rights such as right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**
 
 
• Found in Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36 to 51).
 
• These principles are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• Aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Include provisions for securing a living wage, equitable distribution of resources, right to work, education, public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement, etc.
 
 
 
• **Justiciability:**
 
 
• Refers to the ability of a matter to be adjudicated by a court of law.
 
• Fundamental Rights being justiciable means that individuals can seek redressal from the courts if these rights are violated.
 
 
 
• **Non-justiciable:**
 
 
• Refers to matters that cannot be adjudicated or enforced by the courts.
 
• DPSP being non-justiciable means that while they provide important guidelines for governance, they cannot be legally enforced by the judiciary.
